question: Which of the following is a popular marine fish variety found in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pomfret.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pomfret is a well-known marine (saltwater) fish, widely caught along India's western and eastern coasts and highly valued as food. (पॉम्फ्रेट — समुद्री मछली)

 

• Other important marine fish varieties of India include Bombay duck, Mackerel, Sardine, Hilsa (found in both marine and estuarine waters) and Tuna.

 

• Mrigal, Catla and Rohu are all major carps — they are freshwater fish, extensively cultured in ponds and tanks as part of Indian composite fish culture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has a coastline of about 7,517 km, and marine fisheries are concentrated mainly in Gujarat, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

 

• The Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) is headquartered at Kochi, Kerala.

 

• India is one of the leading fish-producing countries in the world and ranks very high in inland fish production as well.

 

NOTE

 

• Mrigal (Option A): A major Indian freshwater carp, part of the 'three Indian major carps' along with Catla and Rohu.

 

• Catla (Option C): A fast-growing freshwater surface-feeding carp, popular in aquaculture.

 

• Rohu (Option D): A freshwater column-feeder carp, one of the most commonly consumed fish in eastern India.

question: Which of the following environmental cues determined the sex of fertilised egg in few reptiles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Temperature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In several reptiles (such as turtles, crocodiles and some lizards), the sex of the developing embryo is decided not by sex chromosomes but by the incubation temperature of the egg — a phenomenon called Temperature-Dependent Sex Determination (TSD). (तापमान — कुछ सरीसृपों में लिंग निर्धारण)

 

• In many turtle species, warmer nests tend to produce females and cooler nests tend to produce males; in most crocodiles, intermediate temperatures often produce males while the extremes produce females.

 

• This is very different from humans and most mammals, where sex is determined genetically at fertilisation by the X and Y chromosomes (XX = female, XY = male).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Because TSD is climate-sensitive, global warming is a serious conservation concern for turtles and crocodiles — rising nest temperatures can skew hatchling populations heavily towards one sex.

 

• In birds, sex is determined by the ZW system (females are ZW, males are ZZ) — the reverse pattern compared to mammals.

 

• Environmental sex determination is also seen in a few fish and some invertebrates, but is best documented and most exam-relevant in reptiles.

 

NOTE

 

• Water (Option B), Touch (Option C) and Wind velocity (Option D) are not known cues for sex determination in reptiles — only incubation temperature plays this role.

question: The atomic number is defined as the total number of __________ present in the nucleus of an atom.
option_3: neutrons and half of the protons
solution_text:
The correct answer is only protons.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The atomic number (Z) of an element is defined as the total number of protons present in the nucleus of an atom. (परमाणु क्रमांक — प्रोटॉनों की संख्या)

 

• It is the atomic number that uniquely identifies an element and fixes its position in the Modern Periodic Table, which is arranged in order of increasing atomic number.

 

• For a neutral atom, the number of protons also equals the number of electrons, since the atom carries no net charge.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The mass number (A) of an atom is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons (also called nucleons) in the nucleus.

 

• Isotopes of an element have the same atomic number but different mass numbers (i.e., a different number of neutrons).

 

• The nucleus of an atom is held together by the strong nuclear force, which overcomes the electrostatic repulsion between protons.

 

NOTE

 

• Only neutrons (Option B) would instead define a different (non-standard) count, not the atomic number.

 

• Neutrons and half of the protons (Option C) and Protons and neutrons (Option D) describe the mass number, not the atomic number — a common point of confusion in exams.

question: What is the atomic mass of Carbon-13 Isotope?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13 amu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Carbon-13 (¹³C) is an isotope of carbon whose mass number (and hence atomic mass) is 13 amu, since the mass number itself is written as part of the isotope's name. (कार्बन-13 — द्रव्यमान संख्या 13)

 

• Carbon has an atomic number of 6 (6 protons). Carbon-13 therefore has 6 protons and 7 neutrons (13 − 6 = 7) in its nucleus.

 

• Carbon-13 is a stable, naturally occurring isotope, making up about 1.1% of natural carbon; it is widely used in NMR spectroscopy and isotope-labelling studies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Carbon-12 (¹²C), with 6 protons and 6 neutrons, is the most abundant isotope (about 98.9%) and is the standard reference for the atomic mass unit (amu).

 

• Carbon-14 (¹⁴C), with 6 protons and 8 neutrons, is a radioactive isotope used in radiocarbon dating of archaeological and geological samples.

 

• Isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties (same number of protons/electrons) but different physical properties like mass.

 

NOTE

 

• 11 amu (Option A) and 14 amu (Option C) do not correspond to Carbon-13's mass number.

 

• 12 amu (Option D) is the mass number of the most common isotope, Carbon-12, not Carbon-13.

question: Which of the following organisms reproduce by the method of binary fission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leishmania.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Binary fission is a form of asexual reproduction in which a single-celled organism divides into two roughly equal daughter cells. Leishmania, a unicellular protozoan parasite, reproduces by this method. (द्विखंडन — लीशमैनिया)

 

• In binary fission, the parent cell's nucleus divides first (mitotically or by simple splitting), followed by division of the cytoplasm, producing two genetically identical daughter cells.

 

• Other common examples of organisms that reproduce by binary fission are Amoeba, Paramecium and bacteria.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Leishmania is transmitted by the bite of an infected sandfly and causes the disease Leishmaniasis (Kala-azar) in humans.

 

• Butterflies are multicellular animals that reproduce sexually, through fertilisation of eggs by sperm.

 

• Rose and Neem plants are multicellular organisms; while they can also propagate asexually by methods like cutting or budding, their normal reproduction is sexual, and they do not reproduce by binary fission (a process specific to unicellular organisms).

 

NOTE

 

• Butterfly (Option A): Reproduces sexually; undergoes complete metamorphosis (egg → larva → pupa → adult).

 

• Rose plant (Option C): A flowering plant, commonly propagated by stem cuttings, not binary fission.

 

• Neem plant (Option D): A flowering tree, reproduces mainly through seeds, not binary fission.

question: What is the name of the place where bees are kept for commercial honey production?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Apiary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An apiary is a place where beehives are kept for commercial honey production; the scientific rearing of bees for honey and wax is called apiculture (मधुमक्खी पालन).

 

• Apiculture provides not just honey but also beeswax, propolis, royal jelly and bee venom, and bees additionally play a vital role in pollination of crops, boosting agricultural yield.

 

• India is a major honey producer, and important honeybee species reared here include Apis cerana indica, Apis mellifera and Apis dorsata.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similar terms often confused in exams: a place for keeping birds is called an aviary; a tank for keeping fish is an aquarium; a protected area for wildlife is a sanctuary.

 

• The scientific study of bees is called melittology, and the science of rearing silk-worms is called sericulture.

 

• Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) promotes beekeeping and apiculture as a rural livelihood activity in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Aviary (Option A): A large enclosure for keeping birds.

 

• Aquarium (Option B): A tank or enclosure for keeping fish and other aquatic organisms.

 

• Sanctuary (Option D): A protected natural area for the conservation of wild animals.

question: A gun recoils backward when fired. The backward motion of the gun is due to:
option_1: Reaction force of the bullet on the gun
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reaction force of the bullet on the gun.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The recoil of a gun is a direct consequence of Newton's Third Law of Motion: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. (न्यूटन का तीसरा नियम — बंदूक का प्रतिक्षेप)

 

• When the gun exerts a forward action force on the bullet (propelling it out at high speed), the bullet exerts an equal and opposite reaction force on the gun, pushing it backward — this is the recoil.

 

• This event also illustrates the law of conservation of momentum: the total momentum of the (gun + bullet) system before firing is zero, so after firing, the backward momentum of the gun exactly balances the forward momentum of the bullet.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Since the gun is much more massive than the bullet, it recoils with a much smaller velocity than the bullet's forward velocity, even though their momenta are equal in magnitude (mv is the same for both).

 

• The same reaction-force principle explains the working of a rocket: hot gases are expelled backward at high speed, pushing the rocket forward.

 

• Newton's three laws of motion were published in his work *Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica* (1687).

 

NOTE

 

• Air resistance (Option B) and Gravity (Option C) act on the bullet/gun but are not the cause of recoil.

 

• Friction between gun and person (Option D) actually opposes/dampens the recoil motion rather than causing it.

question: Sound waves in air are longitudinal because:
option_1: Particles move along the direction of propagation
option_4: Particles move perpendicular to direction of propagation
solution_text:
The correct answer is Particles move along the direction of propagation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A longitudinal wave is one in which the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth along the same direction in which the wave travels — this is exactly how sound travels in air. (अनुदैर्ध्य तरंग — कणों का कंपन तरंग की दिशा में)

 

• As a sound wave passes through air, it creates alternating regions of compression (particles close together, high pressure) and rarefaction (particles spread apart, low pressure), both along the direction of wave travel.

 

• This is in contrast to a transverse wave, where the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation, such as in light waves or waves on a stretched string.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sound requires a material medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel and cannot pass through vacuum, since there are no particles to vibrate.

 

• Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases, because particles are most closely packed in solids.

 

• Examples of transverse waves include light, water ripples on the surface, and waves on a vibrating string; examples of longitudinal waves include sound waves and P-waves (primary seismic waves).

 

NOTE

 

• Particles move randomly (Option B): Incorrect — the vibration is orderly and along a fixed axis, not random.

 

• Air molecules do not vibrate (Option C): Incorrect — vibration of molecules is exactly what produces and carries the sound wave.

 

• Particles move perpendicular to the direction of propagation (Option D): This describes a transverse, not longitudinal, wave.

question: The magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular loop is directly proportional to _______________.
option_1: the square of the radius of the circular loop
option_2: the current flowing through the loop
option_3: the square of the current flowing through the loop
option_4: inverse of current flowing through the loop
solution_text:
The correct answer is the current flowing through the loop.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The magnetic field at the centre of a current-carrying circular loop is given by B = μ₀I / 2R, where I is the current and R is the radius of the loop. (धारावाही वृत्ताकार पाश — केंद्र पर चुंबकीय क्षेत्र)

 

• From this formula, B is directly proportional to the current (I) flowing through the loop — doubling the current doubles the magnetic field.

 

• The field is inversely proportional to the radius (R), not directly proportional to its square — a smaller loop of the same current produces a stronger field at its centre.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• μ₀ is the permeability of free space, with value 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.

 

• The direction of the magnetic field at the centre of the loop is given by the right-hand thumb rule: if the fingers curl in the direction of current flow, the thumb points in the direction of the field.

 

• For N turns of the coil, the field becomes B = μ₀NI / 2R — directly proportional to the number of turns as well.

 

NOTE

 

• The square of the radius (Option A): Incorrect — the field is inversely (not directly, and not as a square) related to radius.

 

• The square of the current (Option C): Incorrect — the relationship with current is linear (first power), not squared.

 

• Inverse of current (Option D): Incorrect — the field increases, not decreases, as current increases.

question: A concave lens produces an image one-third the size of the object. If the focal length is 12 cm, the object distance is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 24 cm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For a concave (diverging) lens, using the Cartesian sign convention, the focal length is negative: f = −12 cm. The image formed is always virtual, erect and diminished, so magnification m = +1/3.

 

• Using m = v/u, we get v = u/3.

 

• Substituting into the lens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f: 3/u − 1/u = 1/f ⇒ 2/u = 1/f ⇒ u = 2f = 2 × (−12) = −24 cm.

 

• The negative sign simply indicates the object is on the same side as incoming light (as per convention); the object distance is 24 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image lying between the optical centre and the focus, no matter where the object is placed — it never forms a real image.

 

• The power of a concave lens is negative and is measured in dioptres (D), where P = 1/f (in metres).

 

• Concave (diverging) lenses are used to correct myopia (near-sightedness).

 

NOTE

 

• 18 cm (Option A), 36 cm (Option B) and 12 cm (Option D) do not satisfy the lens equation with f = 12 cm and m = 1/3; only u = 24 cm balances both conditions.

question: A charge of 1.5 C is moved through a potential difference. If the work done is 30 J, what is the potential difference between the two points?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 20 V.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Potential difference (V) between two points is defined as the work done (W) per unit charge (Q) moved between those points: V = W/Q. (विभवांतर — प्रति एकांक आवेश किया गया कार्य)

 

• Substituting the given values: V = 30 J ÷ 1.5 C = 20 V.

 

• The SI unit of potential difference is the volt (V), where 1 volt = 1 joule/coulomb.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Electric current (I) is the rate of flow of charge: I = Q/t, measured in amperes (A).

 

• Ohm's Law relates these quantities: V = IR, where R is resistance measured in ohms (Ω).

 

• A voltmeter is used to measure potential difference and is always connected in parallel across the component; an ammeter measures current and is connected in series.

 

NOTE

 

• 25 V (Option A), 30 V (Option B) and 45 V (Option C) would all require a charge different from 1.5 C to be correct — only 20 V satisfies V = W/Q with the given data.

question: In the connective tissue, what is the relative position of the cells with respect to each other?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Far away from each other.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Connective tissue is characterised by cells that are scattered and widely spaced (far away from each other), embedded in a large amount of intercellular matrix (which may be jelly-like, fibrous or solid). (संयोजी ऊतक — कोशिकाएँ दूर-दूर स्थित)

 

• This abundant, non-living matrix (containing fibres like collagen and elastin) is what gives connective tissue its supporting, binding and packing functions throughout the body.

 

• This is in sharp contrast to epithelial tissue, where cells are tightly packed with very little intercellular matrix, forming a continuous protective sheet.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Types of connective tissue include areolar tissue, adipose tissue, bone, cartilage, tendons, ligaments and blood.

 

• Blood is a unique fluid connective tissue, in which the matrix (plasma) is liquid and the cells (RBCs, WBCs, platelets) float within it.

 

• Tendons connect muscle to bone, while ligaments connect bone to bone — both are made of connective tissue rich in collagen fibres.

 

NOTE

 

• Tightly packed (Option A) describes epithelial tissue, not connective tissue.

 

• One above the other (Option B) and Loosely packed (Option D) do not accurately describe the characteristic scattered arrangement of connective tissue cells within their matrix.

question: Which of the following compounds is unsaturated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Propene.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C) or triple bond (C≡C). Propene (C₃H₆) is an alkene, containing one C=C double bond, making it unsaturated. (असंतृप्त यौगिक — द्विआबंध युक्त)

 

• Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes), in contrast, contain only single bonds between carbon atoms and follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

 

• Butane (C₄H₁₀), Methane (CH₄) and Propane (C₃H₈) are all alkanes with only single C–C bonds, so they are all saturated.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alkenes (general formula CₙH₂ₙ) contain a double bond, e.g., ethene (C₂H₄), propene (C₃H₆).

 

• Alkynes (general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂) contain a triple bond, e.g., ethyne/acetylene (C₂H₂).

 

• Unsaturated compounds decolourise bromine water and alkaline KMnO₄ (Baeyer's reagent), a simple test used to distinguish them from saturated compounds.

 

NOTE

 

• Butane (Option A): A saturated alkane, C₄H₁₀.

 

• Methane (Option B): The simplest saturated alkane, CH₄, the main component of natural gas and biogas.

 

• Propane (Option D): A saturated alkane, C₃H₈, commonly used as LPG fuel.

question: If the thrust acting on a surface is constant but the area of contact decreases, the pressure:
solution_text:
The correct answer is increases.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pressure (P) is defined as thrust (force) per unit area: P = F/A. (दाब — प्रति एकांक क्षेत्रफल बल)

 

• If the thrust (F) is kept constant while the area of contact (A) decreases, then since P is inversely proportional to A, the pressure increases.

 

• This is why objects with a sharp/pointed area (like a needle or a knife blade) exert a very high pressure even under a moderate force — the small contact area concentrates the same force intensely.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

 

• Conversely, spreading the same force over a larger area reduces pressure — this is why wide tyres, broad shoes for snow, and wide foundations for buildings are used.

 

• Atmospheric pressure at sea level is about 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa, also expressed as 1 atmosphere.

 

NOTE

 

• Decreases (Option B) would be true only if the area increased, not decreased.

 

• Remains the same (Option C) would only hold if area were unchanged.

 

• Becomes zero (Option D) is incorrect — pressure never becomes zero simply because area shrinks; it in fact rises.

question: Which of the following methods is NOT effective to prevent the corrosion of metals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Exposure to moisture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Corrosion is the gradual deterioration of a metal due to reaction with substances in its environment, especially moisture (water) and oxygen in the air. Exposure to moisture actually promotes corrosion rather than preventing it. (संक्षारण — नमी की उपस्थिति में तेज़)

 

• Rusting of iron, for example, requires both oxygen and moisture; the presence of moisture speeds up the electrochemical reaction that forms iron oxide (rust).

 

• All the other listed methods — painting, galvanisation and sacrificial anodes — work precisely by keeping moisture and oxygen away from the metal surface or by protecting it electrochemically.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Painting creates a physical barrier that prevents oxygen and moisture from reaching the metal surface.

 

• Galvanisation is the coating of iron/steel with a layer of zinc, which is more reactive and corrodes preferentially, protecting the iron underneath.

 

• Sacrificial anode protection uses a more reactive metal (like zinc or magnesium) connected to the metal to be protected; the more reactive metal corrodes first, saving the main structure — commonly used for ships' hulls and pipelines.

 

NOTE

 

• Painting (Option A), Applying sacrificial anodes (Option C) and Galvanisation (Option D) are all genuine, standard corrosion-prevention techniques — the question asks for the method that is NOT effective, which is exposure to moisture.

question:
Read the statements given below and select the correct option.

Statement I: Zinc displaces copper from copper sulphate solution, but copper cannot displace zinc from zinc sulphate solution.

Statement II: Zinc is more reactive than copper in the reactivity series.
option_3: Both statements are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I.
option_4: Both statements are correct, and Statement II correctly explains Statement I.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both statements are correct, and Statement II correctly explains Statement I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I is correct: Zinc, being more reactive, can displace copper from copper sulphate solution in a displacement reaction: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Copper, being less reactive, cannot displace zinc from zinc sulphate solution. (धातु विस्थापन अभिक्रिया)

 

• Statement II is correct: In the reactivity series (activity series) of metals, zinc is placed above copper, confirming zinc is more reactive than copper.

 

• Statement II correctly explains Statement I: A more reactive metal can always displace a less reactive metal from its salt solution — this is precisely the general rule that explains why the displacement in Statement I occurs. Since Statement II gives the underlying reason for Statement I, the two statements are linked, making Option D correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The general order of reactivity (most to least reactive) is often remembered by the mnemonic: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, (H), Cu, Ag, Au — Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Lead, (Hydrogen), Copper, Silver, Gold.

 

• Metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series can displace hydrogen from dilute acids; metals below hydrogen (like copper, silver, gold) cannot.

 

• Displacement reactions are a type of single displacement (or substitution) reaction: A + BX → AX + B, where A is more reactive than B.

 

NOTE

 

• Only statement I (Option A) and Only statement II (Option B) are incomplete — both statements are actually correct.

 

• Both correct but II does not explain I (Option C) is incorrect, because Statement II (zinc's higher reactivity) is in fact exactly why the displacement described in Statement I occurs.

question: Which of the following gases is evolved when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbon dioxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl) reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃, baking soda), it produces sodium chloride, water and carbon dioxide gas: NaHCO₃ + HCl → NaCl + H₂O + CO₂↑. (कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड गैस — सोडियम हाइड्रोजनकार्बोनेट व अम्ल की अभिक्रिया)

 

• This is a classic reaction of all carbonates and hydrogencarbonates (bicarbonates) with acids, always releasing CO₂ gas with brisk effervescence.

 

• The evolved CO₂ can be tested by passing it through lime water (calcium hydroxide solution), which turns milky due to formation of insoluble calcium carbonate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sodium hydrogencarbonate is commonly known as baking soda and is used in cooking, as an antacid, and in fire extinguishers.

 

• The general reaction is: Metal carbonate/hydrogencarbonate + Acid → Salt + Water + Carbon dioxide.

 

• Metals react with acids to release hydrogen gas (e.g., Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂), which is tested by bringing a burning matchstick near the gas — it burns with a pop sound.

 

NOTE

 

• Nitrogen (Option A) and Oxygen (Option B) are not produced in this reaction.

 

• Hydrogen (Option C) is evolved when acids react with reactive metals, not with carbonates or hydrogencarbonates.

question: In the sign convention for lenses, all distances are measured from:
option_3: The optical centre of the lens
solution_text:
The correct answer is The optical centre of the lens.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Cartesian (New Cartesian) sign convention used for lenses, all distances (object distance, image distance, focal length) are measured from the optical centre of the lens. (प्रकाशिक केंद्र — दूरियों का मापन बिंदु)

 

• Distances measured in the direction of the incident light are taken as positive, and those measured against it (opposite to incident light) are taken as negative.

 

• Heights measured upward from the principal axis are positive, and those measured downward are negative.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The optical centre is the central point of a lens through which a light ray passes without any deviation.

 

• For mirrors, by contrast, distances are measured from the pole of the mirror, not from any 'optical centre'.

 

• Under this convention, for a convex lens the focal length is taken as positive, and for a concave lens it is taken as negative.

 

NOTE

 

• The principal axis (Option A) is the reference *line* along which distances are measured, but the *origin point* on that line is the optical centre.

 

• The focus (Option B) and The pole (Option D) are specific points relevant to mirrors and lens geometry respectively, but are not the reference origin for the lens sign convention.

question: What is the need for sexual reproduction in plants?
option_2: To increase genetic variation for better adaptation
option_4: To eliminate the need for pollination
solution_text:
The correct answer is To increase genetic variation for better adaptation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sexual reproduction in plants involves the fusion of male and female gametes, combining genetic material from two parents. This produces offspring with new combinations of genes, increasing genetic variation. (लैंगिक जनन — आनुवंशिक विविधता)

 

• Greater genetic variation gives a population a better chance of having individuals suited to survive changing environmental conditions, diseases, or new predators — improving the species' long-term adaptability and survival.

 

• This is fundamentally different from asexual reproduction, which produces genetically identical offspring (clones) of a single parent, offering no new variation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• In flowering plants, sexual reproduction involves pollination (transfer of pollen from anther to stigma), followed by fertilisation to form a zygote, which develops into a seed.

 

• Asexual reproduction methods in plants include vegetative propagation (cutting, grafting, layering) and budding, which are faster but do not add variation.

 

• Genetic variation produced by sexual reproduction is the raw material on which natural selection acts, driving evolution.

 

NOTE

 

• To produce identical clones (Option A) describes the outcome of asexual, not sexual, reproduction.

 

• To avoid growing flowers (Option C) is incorrect and irrelevant — flowers are the reproductive organs used in sexual reproduction.

 

• To eliminate the need for pollination (Option D) is incorrect — pollination is in fact an essential step of sexual reproduction in flowering plants.

question: If a body falls freely from a height, its potential energy is converted into __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kinetic energy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a body falls freely under gravity, its height above the ground decreases while its speed increases. Its potential energy (energy due to position) is progressively converted into kinetic energy (energy due to motion). (स्थितिज ऊर्जा का गतिज ऊर्जा में रूपांतरण)

 

• This is a direct application of the law of conservation of mechanical energy: in the absence of air resistance, the total mechanical energy (PE + KE) of the falling body remains constant throughout the fall.

 

• At the highest point, the body has maximum PE and zero KE; just before hitting the ground, it has maximum KE and (taking ground as reference) zero PE.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Potential energy formula: PE = mgh (mass × acceleration due to gravity × height).

 

• Kinetic energy formula: KE = ½mv² (half × mass × velocity squared).

 

• In real free fall, a small fraction of energy is lost as heat and sound due to air resistance, but in the ideal (frictionless) case, PE converts entirely into KE.

 

NOTE

 

• Chemical energy (Option B) is not relevant to simple mechanical free fall.

 

• Sound energy (Option C) and Thermal energy (Option D) may appear as minor losses due to air resistance, but they are not the *main* form the potential energy converts into — that is kinetic energy.

question: Which of the following cell organelles releases Adenosine Tri Phosphate (ATP) molecules needed for life activities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mitochondria.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mitochondria are the cell organelles where cellular respiration occurs, producing ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) — the energy currency used to power all life activities of the cell. They are hence called the 'powerhouse of the cell'. (माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया — कोशिका का ऊर्जा गृह)

 

• Mitochondria have a double membrane; the inner membrane is folded into structures called cristae, which increase surface area for ATP-producing reactions.

 

• Mitochondria contain their own DNA and ribosomes, and are believed to have originated from free-living bacteria through endosymbiosis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vacuoles are storage sacs for water, food, waste, or (in plant cells) for maintaining turgor pressure.

 

• The Golgi apparatus packages and modifies proteins and lipids, and is involved in the formation of lysosomes.

 

• Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes and are called the 'suicide bags' of the cell, as they can digest worn-out cell components and even the whole cell.

 

NOTE

 

• Vacuoles (Option B): Function mainly in storage, not ATP production.

 

• Golgi apparatus (Option C): Functions in packaging and secretion, not respiration.

 

• Lysosomes (Option D): Function in intracellular digestion, not energy generation.

question: Which of the following represents an end product of anaerobic respiration in animals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lactic acid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Anaerobic respiration in animal (muscle) cells occurs when oxygen supply is insufficient, breaking down glucose without oxygen to produce lactic acid and release a small amount of energy. (अवायवीय श्वसन — लैक्टिक अम्ल का निर्माण)

 

• This commonly occurs in muscle cells during vigorous exercise, when the demand for energy outpaces the oxygen supply; the accumulation of lactic acid causes muscle cramps and fatigue.

 

• In contrast, aerobic respiration (which requires oxygen) breaks glucose down completely into carbon dioxide and water, releasing much more energy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Overall word equation for anaerobic respiration in muscles: Glucose → Lactic acid + Energy (small amount).

 

• In yeast (and some microorganisms), anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and carbon dioxide instead — this process is called fermentation, used in brewing and baking.

 

• Aerobic respiration equation: Glucose + Oxygen → Carbon dioxide + Water + Energy (large amount).

 

NOTE

 

• Glucose (Option A) is the *starting material* (substrate) of respiration, not its end product.

 

• Oxygen (Option B) is required for aerobic respiration, and is not involved in (or produced by) anaerobic respiration in animals.

 

• Carbon monoxide (Option C) is a toxic gas unrelated to normal cellular respiration.

question: The Law of conservation of mass states that:
option_1: volume can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction
option_2: mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction
option_3: pressure can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction
option_4: temperature can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction
solution_text:
The correct answer is mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Law of Conservation of Mass states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction — the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products. (द्रव्यमान संरक्षण का नियम)

 

• This law was established through careful experiments by the French chemist Antoine Lavoisier, often called the 'Father of Modern Chemistry'.

 

• It forms the basis for balancing chemical equations, ensuring the number of atoms of each element is equal on both the reactant and product sides.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related law: the Law of Constant (Definite) Proportions, given by Joseph Proust, states that a chemical compound always contains the same elements combined in a fixed proportion by mass, regardless of its source.

 

• Mass conservation applies strictly to non-nuclear (chemical) reactions; in nuclear reactions, a tiny amount of mass can convert to energy as per Einstein's E = mc².

 

• These conservation laws laid the foundation of modern stoichiometry in chemistry.

 

NOTE

 

• Volume (Option A), pressure (Option C) and temperature (Option D) are not conserved quantities in a chemical reaction in the way mass is — volume and pressure of gases can very much change, and temperature can rise or fall (exothermic/endothermic reactions).

question: A car travels 100 km at an average speed of 50 km h⁻¹ and immediately returns along the same route covering the distance in 1 hour. What is the average speed of the car for the entire journey in m s⁻¹?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18.52 m s⁻¹ (as printed in the source, this appears truncated as B).52 m s-1).

 

GIVEN

 

• One-way distance = 100 km, covered at 50 km/h. Return trip covers the same 100 km in 1 hour.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Time for the onward journey = Distance ÷ Speed = 100 ÷ 50 = 2 hours.

 

• Time for the return journey = 1 hour (given directly).

 

• Total distance covered = 100 + 100 = 200 km = 200,000 m.

 

• Total time taken = 2 + 1 = 3 hours = 10,800 seconds.

 

• Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time = 200,000 ÷ 10,800 = 18.5185... ≈ 18.52 m/s, which matches option B (printed in the source with its leading digits cut off as "B).52 m s-1").

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Average speed for a round trip = Total distance ÷ Total time, never the simple average of the two speeds.

 

• In km/h first: 200 km ÷ 3 h = 66.67 km/h; converting to m/s: 66.67 × (5/18) ≈ 18.52 m/s.

 

NOTE

 

• A very common mistake is to average the two speeds directly (e.g. taking (50+100)/2); this is wrong whenever the *times* for each leg are different — always go back to total distance ÷ total time.

 

• Note the printed options in the source PDF are truncated (their leading digits are missing, e.g. "B).52" instead of "18.52") — this is reproduced here exactly as it appears in the original question paper.

question: The reactivity series, also known as the activity series, is a list of metals arranged in order of their:
solution_text:
The correct answer is decreasing reactivity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The reactivity series (activity series) is a list of metals arranged in the order of decreasing reactivity — the most reactive metal is placed at the top and the least reactive at the bottom. (सक्रियता श्रेणी — घटती अभिक्रियाशीलता के क्रम में)

 

• A common mnemonic for the order (most to least reactive) is: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, (H), Cu, Ag, Au — Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Lead, (Hydrogen), Copper, Silver, Gold.

 

• A metal placed higher in the series can displace a metal placed lower from its salt solution, and reacts more vigorously with acids and water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Metals above hydrogen in the series can liberate hydrogen gas from dilute acids; metals below hydrogen (Cu, Ag, Au) generally cannot.

 

• Gold and platinum are among the least reactive metals, which is why they are found in their native (free) state in nature and are used in jewellery.

 

• Potassium and sodium are so reactive that they react vigorously even with cold water and are stored under kerosene oil to prevent contact with air/moisture.

 

NOTE

 

• Increasing reactivity (Option A) is the reverse of the actual arrangement.

 

• First decreasing, then increasing (Option C) and First increasing, then decreasing (Option D) describe non-monotonic patterns that do not match the standard reactivity series, which is a single decreasing order.

question: If X − Y = 20 and XY = 12, then find the value of X² + Y².
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 424.

 

GIVEN

 

• X − Y = 20 and XY = 12.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the identity: (X − Y)² = X² + Y² − 2XY.

 

• So X² + Y² = (X − Y)² + 2XY.

 

• Substitute values: X² + Y² = 20² + 2(12) = 400 + 24 = 424.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever (a − b) and ab are given, directly use a² + b² = (a − b)² + 2ab — no need to solve for a and b individually.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse this with (X + Y)² = X² + Y² + 2XY — the sign of the 2XY term depends on whether the sum or difference is given.

question: The vertices of a quadrilateral are A(2,3), B(5,7), C(10,6), and D(7,2). Find the area of the quadrilateral ABCD.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 23 sq. units.

 

GIVEN

 

• Vertices (in order): A(2,3), B(5,7), C(10,6), D(7,2).

 

SOLUTION (Shoelace formula)

 

• Area = ½|（x_A y_B − x_B y_A) + (x_B y_C − x_C y_B) + (x_C y_D − x_D y_C) + (x_D y_A − x_A y_D)|.

 

• (x_A y_B − x_B y_A) = 2×7 − 5×3 = 14 − 15 = −1.

 

• (x_B y_C − x_C y_B) = 5×6 − 10×7 = 30 − 70 = −40.

 

• (x_C y_D − x_D y_C) = 10×2 − 7×6 = 20 − 42 = −22.

 

• (x_D y_A − x_A y_D) = 7×3 − 2×2 = 21 − 4 = 17.

 

• Sum = −1 − 40 − 22 + 17 = −46. Area = ½ × |−46| = 23 sq. units.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Shoelace formula: Area = ½|Σ(x_i y_{i+1} − x_{i+1} y_i)|, taking vertices strictly in order (clockwise or anticlockwise) around the polygon.

 

NOTE

 

• Always keep the vertices in the order given (do not reorder them), since the shoelace method depends on tracing the polygon's boundary in sequence.

question: Seema bought a microwave oven for ₹7,500 and sold it for ₹8,750. Find Seema's profit percentage. (Round off your answer to two decimal places.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 16.67% (printed in the source as "A).67%").

 

GIVEN

 

• Cost Price (CP) = ₹7,500; Selling Price (SP) = ₹8,750.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Profit = SP − CP = 8,750 − 7,500 = ₹1,250.

 

• Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (1,250 ÷ 7,500) × 100 = 16.666...% ≈ 16.67%, matching option A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Profit% = (1,250/7,500) × 100 = (1/6) × 100 = 16.67% — recognising 1,250/7,500 simplifies to 1/6 saves calculation time.

 

NOTE

 

• The options in the source PDF are printed with their leading digits missing (e.g. "A).67%" instead of "16.67%") — reproduced here exactly as in the original question paper; the true value behind option A is 16.67%.

question: The marked price of an item is set at 51% above its cost price. If the merchant sells the item at 8% below the marked price, his profit percentage (rounded off to 1 decimal place) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 38.9% (printed in the source as "D).9%").

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked Price (MP) = 51% above Cost Price (CP); Selling Price (SP) = 8% below MP.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let CP = 100. Then MP = 100 + 51% of 100 = 151.

 

• SP = MP − 8% of MP = 151 × 0.92 = 138.92.

 

• Profit% = (SP − CP) = 138.92 − 100 = 38.92%, which rounds to 38.9%, matching option D.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine successive percentage changes multiplicatively: Net% change = 151% × 92% (of CP) − 100% = 1.51 × 0.92 × 100 − 100 = 138.92 − 100 = 38.92% ≈ 38.9%.

 

NOTE

 

• The options in the source PDF are printed with their leading digits missing (e.g. "D).9%" instead of "38.9%") — reproduced here exactly as in the original question paper; the true value behind option D is 38.9%.

question: What is the simple interest on a sum of ₹3,500, if the rate of interest for the first 6 years is 8% per annum and for the last 3 years is 3% per annum?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹1,995.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal (P) = ₹3,500. Rate = 8% p.a. for the first 6 years, then 3% p.a. for the next 3 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• SI for the first 6 years = (P × R × T)/100 = (3500 × 8 × 6)/100 = ₹1,680.

 

• SI for the next 3 years = (3500 × 3 × 3)/100 = ₹315.

 

• Total simple interest = 1,680 + 315 = ₹1,995.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When the rate changes over different periods, simply calculate the interest for each period separately using SI = PRT/100 and add them — the principal stays the same throughout since it's simple (not compound) interest.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not apply compound interest logic here — with simple interest, interest is always computed on the original principal, never on accumulated interest.

question: The number of prime numbers lying between 440 and 452 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• Range: numbers strictly between 440 and 452.

 

SOLUTION

 

• List numbers 441 to 451 and check each for primality: 441 (=21×21, not prime), 442 (even), 443 (prime — not divisible by 2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19), 444 (even), 445 (÷5), 446 (even), 447 (÷3, since 4+4+7=15), 448 (even), 449 (prime — not divisible by any prime up to √449≈21.2), 450 (even), 451 (=11×41, not prime).

 

• Primes found: 443 and 449 — a total of 2 primes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• To test if a number N is prime, it's enough to check divisibility by primes up to √N. For numbers near 450, check only 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19 (since 19² = 361 < 450 < 441 = 21²).

 

NOTE

 

• Always eliminate even numbers and multiples of 5 first — this quickly narrows the list of candidates to check.

question: The length of each of the two equal sides of an isosceles triangle is 78 cm, and the length of its base is 60 cm. Find the area (in cm²) of the triangle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 2160 cm².

 

GIVEN

 

• Equal sides = 78 cm each; base = 60 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The altitude from the apex bisects the base into two halves of 30 cm each, forming a right triangle with hypotenuse 78 cm and base 30 cm.

 

• Height = √(78² − 30²) = √(6084 − 900) = √5184 = 72 cm.

 

• Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 60 × 72 = 2160 cm².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For an isosceles triangle with equal side 'a' and base 'b', Area = (b/4)√(4a² − b²) = (60/4)√(4×78² − 60²) = 15 × √(24336 − 3600) = 15 × √20736 = 15 × 144 = 2160 cm².

 

NOTE

 

• The altitude of an isosceles triangle always bisects the base perpendicularly — this is the key geometric fact that lets you form a right triangle and apply the Pythagorean theorem.

question: 2 men or 9 women can do a job in 9 days. 2 men work for 5 days and leave. The number of women required to complete the remaining work in 9 days is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• 2 men can finish the job in 9 days, and so can 9 women; 2 men work for only 5 days, then leave.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total work = 2 men × 9 days = 18 man-days. Also, total work = 9 women × 9 days = 81 woman-days.

 

• So 18 man-days = 81 woman-days ⇒ 1 man-day = 4.5 woman-days.

 

• Work done by 2 men in 5 days = 2 × 5 = 10 man-days = 10 × 4.5 = 45 woman-days.

 

• Remaining work = 81 − 45 = 36 woman-days, to be finished in 9 days.

 

• Women required = 36 ÷ 9 = 4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert everything to a common unit (man-days or woman-days) using the equivalence given (2 men = 9 women in terms of total work), then apply Work = Rate × Time directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always find the equivalence ratio between the two types of workers (here, 2 men = 9 women, i.e., 1 man = 4.5 women) before mixing them in a single calculation.

question: If 30% of 40% of 5/9 of a number is 704, find the number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 10,560.

 

GIVEN

 

• 30% of 40% of (5/9) of a number N = 704.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert to a single fraction: 30% × 40% × (5/9) = 0.3 × 0.4 × 5/9 = 0.12 × 5/9 = 0.6/9 = 1/15.

 

• So (1/15) × N = 704.

 

• N = 704 × 15 = 10,560.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Multiply all the given fractions/percentages together first to get one combined fraction (here 1/15), then simply multiply the given value by the reciprocal (×15) to find N.

 

NOTE

 

• Convert percentages to fractions (30% = 3/10, 40% = 2/5) before multiplying — this avoids decimal errors and keeps the arithmetic clean.

question: 1/20 is what percentage of 2/50?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 125%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Find what percentage 1/20 is of 2/50.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1/20 = 0.05, and 2/50 = 0.04.

 

• Required percentage = (0.05 ÷ 0.04) × 100 = 125%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Percentage = (First fraction ÷ Second fraction) × 100 = (1/20 × 50/2) × 100 = (50/40) × 100 = 125%.

 

NOTE

 

• "A is what % of B" always means (A/B) × 100 — make sure to divide the first quantity by the second, not the other way around.

question: If an item marked at ₹758 is sold for ₹256, then what is the discount percentage? (Round off the answer to two decimal places)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 66.23% (printed in the source as "A).23%").

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked Price (MP) = ₹758; Selling Price (SP) = ₹256.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Discount = MP − SP = 758 − 256 = ₹502.

 

• Discount% = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (502 ÷ 758) × 100 = 66.2269...% ≈ 66.23%, matching option A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Discount% = ((MP − SP)/MP) × 100 — always divide by the marked price, not the selling price, when finding discount percentage.

 

NOTE

 

• The options in the source PDF are printed with their leading digits missing (e.g. "A).23%" instead of "66.23%") — reproduced here exactly as in the original question paper; the true value behind option A is 66.23%.

question: R pays ₹20 with ₹2 and ₹5 coins. If at least one coin of each denomination is used in paying the amount, then the number of ₹2 coins used is _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 5.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total amount = ₹20, paid using only ₹2 and ₹5 coins, with at least one coin of each type.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the number of ₹2 coins = a, and ₹5 coins = b. Then 2a + 5b = 20, with a ≥ 1 and b ≥ 1 (whole numbers).

 

• Try b = 1: 2a = 15 → a is not an integer. Reject.

 

• Try b = 2: 2a = 10 → a = 5. Valid (both a, b ≥ 1).

 

• Try b = 3: 2a = 5 → not an integer. Reject. Higher b values make 2a negative.

 

• The only valid solution is a = 5, b = 2, so the number of ₹2 coins = 5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since 5b must leave an even remainder when subtracted from 20 (so that 2a is a whole even number), b must be even. The smallest valid even b (≥1) is b = 2, giving a = 5 directly.

 

NOTE

 

• In coin/denomination problems, always check the parity (odd/even) constraint first — it quickly rules out invalid combinations.

question: One pipe can fill a tank in 6 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 12 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 3 minutes.

 

GIVEN

 

• Filling pipe: fills the tank in 6 minutes. Emptying pipe: empties a full tank in 12 minutes. Both are opened together on an empty tank.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Filling rate = 1/6 tank per minute. Emptying rate = 1/12 tank per minute.

 

• Combined (net) rate = 1/6 − 1/12 = 2/12 − 1/12 = 1/12 tank per minute.

 

• Time to fill 1/4 of the tank = (1/4) ÷ (1/12) = (1/4) × 12 = 3 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net rate = 1/(fill time) − 1/(empty time); once you have the net rate, Time = Required fraction ÷ Net rate.

 

NOTE

 

• Since the emptying pipe works against the filling pipe, always subtract the rates (not add) when both pipes work simultaneously in opposite roles.

question: A train overtakes two persons walking along a railway track. The first one walks at 5.4 km/hr. The other one walks at 18 km/hr. The train needs 30 and 44 seconds, respectively, to overtake them. What is the speed of the train, if both the persons walking in the same direction as the train?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 45 km/hr.

 

GIVEN

 

• Person 1 walks at 5.4 km/h, overtaken in 30 s. Person 2 walks at 18 km/h, overtaken in 44 s. Both walk in the same direction as the train.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let train speed = v km/h and train length = L metres. Since the train overtakes people walking in the same direction, relative speed = (v − person's speed).

 

• For person 1: L = (v − 5.4) × (5/18) × 30.

 

• For person 2: L = (v − 18) × (5/18) × 44.

 

• Equating the two expressions for L: (v − 5.4) × 30 = (v − 18) × 44.

 

• 30v − 162 = 44v − 792 ⇒ 792 − 162 = 44v − 30v ⇒ 630 = 14v ⇒ v = 45 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since the train's length L is the same in both cases, equate (Relative speed₁ × Time₁) = (Relative speed₂ × Time₂) directly, in consistent units, and solve for the unknown train speed.

 

NOTE

 

• When a train overtakes a person walking in the same direction, always use (train speed − person's speed) as the relative speed — for someone walking in the opposite direction, the speeds would be added instead.

question:
Calculate the mode of the following data. (Round off to two decimal places)

Marks: 4-8, 8-12, 12-16, 16-20, 20-24, 24-28, 28-32, 32-36

No. of Students: 9, 12, 18, 34, 26, 20, 12, 7
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 18.67 (printed in the source with all four options showing only "X).67" — a rendering issue in the original paper; the correct value is 18.67, corresponding to Option A).

 

GIVEN

 

• Class intervals of width 4, with frequencies 9, 12, 18, 34, 26, 20, 12, 7 for the eight classes from 4-8 up to 32-36.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The modal class is the class with the highest frequency: 16-20, with frequency f₁ = 34.

 

• Here: L (lower boundary of modal class) = 16, f₀ (frequency of preceding class, 12-16) = 18, f₂ (frequency of succeeding class, 20-24) = 26, h (class width) = 4.

 

• Mode = L + [(f₁ − f₀) / (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h = 16 + [(34 − 18) / (68 − 18 − 26)] × 4.

 

• = 16 + [16/24] × 4 = 16 + (2/3) × 4 = 16 + 2.6667 = 18.67 (rounded to 2 decimal places).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always identify the modal class first by simply spotting the highest frequency; then plug values directly into Mode = L + [(f₁−f₀)/(2f₁−f₀−f₂)]×h — no need to compute anything for the non-adjacent classes.

 

NOTE

 

• All four options in the original source PDF are printed identically as "X).67" due to a rendering issue (their distinguishing leading digits are missing); the actual, correctly computed mode is 18.67, which is Option A as marked correct in the answer key.

question: The sides of a triangle are 102 cm, 154 cm, and 80 cm. What is the length (in cm) of its altitude corresponding to the side with a length of 154 cm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 48 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• Triangle with sides 102 cm, 154 cm and 80 cm; find the altitude on the side of length 154 cm.

 

SOLUTION (Heron's formula)

 

• Semi-perimeter s = (102 + 154 + 80)/2 = 336/2 = 168 cm.

 

• Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] = √[168 × (168−102) × (168−154) × (168−80)] = √[168 × 66 × 14 × 88].

 

• 168 × 66 = 11,088; 14 × 88 = 1,232; 11,088 × 1,232 = 13,660,416.

 

• Area = √13,660,416 = 3,696 cm².

 

• Altitude on side 154 cm = (2 × Area) ÷ base = (2 × 3,696) ÷ 154 = 7,392 ÷ 154 = 48 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once the area is found by Heron's formula, the altitude on any side is simply 2×Area ÷ that side — no need for a separate geometric construction.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check Heron's formula computation by grouping factors sensibly (e.g. 168×66 and 14×88 separately) to avoid arithmetic slips with large numbers.

question: The income of Raman is ₹25,000. He saves 25.5% of his income. If his income increases by 20% and expenditure increases by 40%, then his savings will:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. decrease by ₹2,450.

 

GIVEN

 

• Income = ₹25,000; Savings = 25.5% of income. New income = old income + 20%; new expenditure = old expenditure + 40%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Savings = 25.5% of 25,000 = ₹6,375.

 

• Expenditure = Income − Savings = 25,000 − 6,375 = ₹18,625.

 

• New income = 25,000 × 1.20 = ₹30,000.

 

• New expenditure = 18,625 × 1.40 = ₹26,075.

 

• New savings = New income − New expenditure = 30,000 − 26,075 = ₹3,925.

 

• Change in savings = 3,925 − 6,375 = −₹2,450, i.e. savings decrease by ₹2,450.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always split income into savings and expenditure first, apply the respective percentage change to each part separately, and then find the new savings by subtraction — do not apply a single blended percentage to total income.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is to assume savings simply change by the same percentage as income; but since savings and expenditure change by *different* percentages, they must be tracked separately.

question: The ratio of the ages of John and James will be 8 : 7 after 8 years. If the difference between their ages is 5 years, find the present age of James.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 27 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• After 8 years, John : James = 8 : 7. The difference between their present ages is 5 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let John's age after 8 years = 8x and James's age after 8 years = 7x.

 

• Since the age difference stays constant over time: 8x − 7x = 5 ⇒ x = 5.

 

• James's age after 8 years = 7x = 7 × 5 = 35 years.

 

• James's present age = 35 − 8 = 27 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The difference in ages never changes with time, so the difference of ratio parts (8x − 7x = x) can be directly equated to the given age difference — this instantly gives the value of x.

 

NOTE

 

• Always remember to subtract the number of years added (here, 8) at the end to get back to the present age, since the ratio was given for a future point in time.

question: The unit prices of lemon chocolate and strawberry chocolate are in the ratio 28:26, and a family consumes them in the ratio 15:14 by quantity. Find the ratio of expenditure on strawberry chocolate to that on lemon chocolate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 13 : 15.

 

GIVEN

 

• Price (lemon : strawberry) = 28 : 26 = 14 : 13. Quantity consumed (lemon : strawberry) = 15 : 14.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Expenditure = Price × Quantity.

 

• Expenditure on lemon ∝ 14 × 15 = 210.

 

• Expenditure on strawberry ∝ 13 × 14 = 182.

 

• Required ratio (strawberry : lemon) = 182 : 210. Dividing both by their HCF 14: 182÷14 = 13, 210÷14 = 15.

 

• Ratio = 13 : 15.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Expenditure ratio = (Price ratio) × (Quantity ratio), multiplied term-by-term, then simplified to lowest terms.

 

NOTE

 

• Always simplify the price ratio (28:26 → 14:13) before multiplying — it keeps the numbers smaller and reduces the chance of arithmetic error.

question: From a point on the ground, the angle of elevation to the top of a tower is θ such that tanθ = 3/4. Find the sine of angle θ.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 3/5.

 

GIVEN

 

• tan θ = 3/4.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since tan θ = Opposite/Adjacent = 3/4, take Opposite = 3 units and Adjacent = 4 units.

 

• Hypotenuse = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 units (recognising the 3-4-5 Pythagorean triplet).

 

• sin θ = Opposite/Hypotenuse = 3/5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever tan θ = p/q is given, instantly recognise the right triangle with legs p, q and hypotenuse √(p²+q²); then sin θ = p/√(p²+q²) and cos θ = q/√(p²+q²) can be read off directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Memorising common Pythagorean triplets (3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25) makes such trigonometry questions much faster to solve.

question:
Simplify the following.

(2x³y⁵z) × (5xy⁶z²) ÷ (15x²yz²)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 2x²y¹⁰z/3.

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: (2x³y⁵z) × (5xy⁶z²) ÷ (15x²yz²).

 

SOLUTION

 

• First multiply the numerator terms: (2x³y⁵z) × (5xy⁶z²) = (2×5) x^(3+1) y^(5+6) z^(1+2) = 10 x⁴y¹¹z³.

 

• Now divide by (15x²yz²): (10/15) × x^(4−2) × y^(11−1) × z^(3−2) = (2/3) x²y¹⁰z.

 

• Result = 2x²y¹⁰z/3.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Handle coefficients and each variable's exponent separately: add exponents when multiplying, subtract when dividing — this avoids errors from tracking everything together.

 

NOTE

 

• Always simplify the numerical coefficient (10/15 = 2/3) to its lowest terms as the final step.

question: A train, 1195 m-long, is running at a speed of 23 m/s. If it takes 72 seconds to cross a tunnel, then find the length of the tunnel.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 461 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train length = 1,195 m; speed = 23 m/s; time to cross the tunnel = 72 s.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Distance covered while crossing the tunnel = Speed × Time = 23 × 72 = 1,656 m.

 

• This distance equals (Length of train + Length of tunnel), since the train must travel its own length plus the tunnel's length to completely cross it.

 

• Length of tunnel = 1,656 − 1,195 = 461 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 'crossing a tunnel/platform/bridge' problems: (Speed × Time) = (Train length + Object length), so Object length = Speed×Time − Train length.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse 'crossing a tunnel' with 'crossing a pole/man' — crossing a stationary point person needs only the train's own length, but crossing an extended object like a tunnel needs the train length plus the tunnel length.

question: A class of 43 students took a Physics test. 10 students had an average score of 99. The other students had an average score of 55. What is the average score (rounded off to one decimal place) of the whole class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 65.2 (printed in the source as "D).2").

 

GIVEN

 

• 43 students total. 10 students average 99; remaining (43−10 = 33) students average 55.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total score of first group = 10 × 99 = 990.

 

• Total score of remaining 33 students = 33 × 55 = 1,815.

 

• Combined total score = 990 + 1,815 = 2,805.

 

• Average of the whole class = 2,805 ÷ 43 = 65.2326... ≈ 65.2, matching option D.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combined average = (Sum of Group 1 + Sum of Group 2) ÷ (Total count) — always convert averages back into totals first, combine, then divide once at the end.

 

NOTE

 

• The options in the source PDF are printed with their leading digits missing (e.g. "D).2" instead of "65.2") — reproduced here exactly as in the original question paper; the true value behind option D is 65.2.

question: The sum of three numbers is 4512. If the ratio between the first and second numbers is 16 : 9 and that between the second and third is 15 : 21, then find the difference between the first and third number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 408.

 

GIVEN

 

• First : Second = 16 : 9. Second : Third = 15 : 21 = 5 : 7. Sum of all three numbers = 4512.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Make the 'Second' term equal in both ratios: First:Second = 16:9 = 80:45 (× 5); Second:Third = 5:7 = 45:63 (× 9).

 

• Combined ratio First : Second : Third = 80 : 45 : 63. Sum of ratio parts = 80 + 45 + 63 = 188.

 

• Value of 1 part = 4512 ÷ 188 = 24.

 

• First number = 80 × 24 = 1,920. Third number = 63 × 24 = 1,512.

 

• Difference = 1,920 − 1,512 = 408.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Directly find the difference in ratio parts: (80 − 63) = 17 parts. Difference = 17 × 24 = 408.

 

NOTE

 

• When combining two ratios sharing a common term (here, 'Second'), always scale both ratios so that the common term has the same value before combining into a single three-part ratio.

question: A garrison of 1,200 men has provisions for 12 days. How long (in days) will the provisions last if the garrison is increased to 1,800 men?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 8 days.

 

GIVEN

 

• 1,200 men have provisions for 12 days. Garrison increases to 1,800 men.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total provisions (in man-days) = 1,200 × 12 = 14,400 man-days.

 

• With 1,800 men, the number of days the same provisions will last = 14,400 ÷ 1,800 = 8 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Men and Days are inversely proportional for a fixed amount of provisions: M₁D₁ = M₂D₂ ⇒ 1200 × 12 = 1800 × D₂ ⇒ D₂ = 14400/1800 = 8.

 

NOTE

 

• More men consuming the same fixed provisions will always make them last for fewer days — always sanity-check that your answer is smaller than the original duration when the number of consumers increases.

question: If each of the digits in the number 47315628 is arranged in ascending order from left to right, then the position(s) of how many digits will remain unchanged as compared to that in the original number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Four.

 

GIVEN

 

• Number: 4 7 3 1 5 6 2 8 (positions 1 to 8).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Arrange the digits in ascending order: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8.

 

• Compare position by position with the original 4 7 3 1 5 6 2 8:

 

• Position 1: 4 vs 1 (different); Position 2: 7 vs 2 (different); Position 3: 3 vs 3 (same); Position 4: 1 vs 4 (different); Position 5: 5 vs 5 (same); Position 6: 6 vs 6 (same); Position 7: 2 vs 7 (different); Position 8: 8 vs 8 (same).

 

• Positions that remain unchanged: 3, 5, 6 and 8 — a total of four digits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Write the original and the sorted sequence one below the other, then simply count the columns where both rows match — no need for any other calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Be careful to compare digit-by-digit at the same position, not just check whether a digit appears somewhere in both sequences (every digit does, since it's simply re-ordered).

question: Mr. Z starts from Point A and drives 14 km towards the North. He then takes a left turn, drives 19 km, then turns left and drives 30 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 21 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 16 km, and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only, unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 2 km to the west.

 

GIVEN

 

• Starting at A, facing North: 14 km North → left turn, 19 km → left turn, 30 km → left turn, 21 km → left turn, 16 km, stopping at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take North as +y, East as +x. Starting direction: North.

 

• Leg 1: 14 km North → position (0, 14).

 

• Left turn from North → facing West. Leg 2: 19 km West → position (−19, 14).

 

• Left turn from West → facing South. Leg 3: 30 km South → position (−19, −16).

 

• Left turn from South → facing East. Leg 4: 21 km East → position (2, −16).

 

• Left turn from East → facing North. Leg 5: 16 km North → position (2, 0).

 

• So Point P is at (2, 0), i.e. 2 km east of the starting line through A, but at the same north-south level as A (0,0).

 

• To go from P(2,0) back to A(0,0), Z must move 2 km in the west direction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the net East-West and net North-South displacement (add distances in the same direction, cancel opposite directions) rather than plotting every intermediate point — here North-South legs (14N, 30S, 16N) net to 0, and East-West legs (19W, 21E) net to 2 km East of A, so the return path is simply 2 km West.

 

NOTE

 

• With a person facing North, a sequence of left turns cycles through North → West → South → East → North; always track which compass direction each 'left turn' actually produces before adding up distances.

question: In a certain code language, 'she play guiter' is coded as 'so tn yw' and 'play chess daily' is coded as 'nj bg so'. How is 'play' coded in the given language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. so.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'she play guiter' → 'so tn yw'; 'play chess daily' → 'nj bg so'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The word 'play' is common to both statements.

 

• Compare the two code strings 'so tn yw' and 'nj bg so' — the code word common to both is 'so'.

 

• Therefore, the code for 'play' must be 'so'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In such coding-decoding puzzles, always find the word that repeats across two statements and match it with the code word that repeats across the corresponding coded strings.

 

NOTE

 

• This method only works reliably when exactly one word (and correspondingly one code word) is common between the two given statements — here that is uniquely 'play' and 'so'.

question:
In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic.

TIPS - PTIS - SPIT

LOST - SLOT - TSOL
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. SPIN - ISPN - NIPS.

 

GIVEN

 

• TIPS → PTIS → SPIT and LOST → SLOT → TSOL follow the same hidden logic.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Step 1 (word1 → word2): the 3rd letter moves to the front, and the other two of the first three letters shift right; the 4th letter stays fixed. E.g., T-I-P-S → P-T-I-S (P, originally 3rd, comes to 1st; T,I shift right; S stays last).

 

• Step 2 (word2 → word3): the 4th letter moves to the front, the (new) 1st letter moves to 2nd, the (new) 4th position now takes the (new) 2nd letter, and the 3rd letter stays fixed. E.g., P-T-I-S → S-P-I-T (S, from 4th, comes to 1st; P moves to 2nd; T moves to 4th; I stays 3rd).

 

• Check with Option D: SPIN (S-P-I-N). Step 1: 3rd letter I moves to front, others shift: I,S,P,N = ISPN ✓ matches the given word2.

 

• Step 2 on ISPN (I-S-P-N): 4th letter N moves to front, I moves to 2nd, P stays 3rd, S moves to 4th: N,I,P,S = NIPS ✓ matches the given word3.

 

• Both transformations match exactly for Option D.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Test each option by mentally applying the same two-step letter-shuffle rule observed in the examples; the option is correct only if BOTH transformations (word1→word2 AND word2→word3) match — checking just the first transformation can still eliminate most wrong options quickly (e.g., BOND→OBND fails the rule already, since the correct step-1 result would be NBOD, not OBND).

 

NOTE

 

• In such triad-analogy questions, always verify the pattern using both steps of the given examples before finalising an option — some distractor options may satisfy only the first step but break at the second.

question: QN 3 is related to RJ −12 in a certain way. In the same way, HE 7 is related to IA −8. To which of the given options is LI 11 related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ME −4.

 

GIVEN

 

• QN 3 → RJ −12, and HE 7 → IA −8; find the pair related to LI 11 the same way.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Letter pattern: In each pair, the 1st letter moves +1 place forward in the alphabet, and the 2nd letter moves −4 places back. Check: Q(17)+1=R(18) ✓, N(14)−4=J(10) ✓; H(8)+1=I(9) ✓, E(5)−4=A(1) ✓.

 

• Apply to LI: L(12)+1 = M(13); I(9)−4 = E(5). So the letters become ME.

 

• Number pattern: each given number decreases by a constant 15: 3 − 15 = −12 ✓; 7 − 15 = −8 ✓.

 

• Apply to 11: 11 − 15 = −4.

 

• So LI 11 is related to ME −4.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split coded-pair questions like this into two independent sub-patterns — one for the letters (using alphabet-position shifts) and one for the numbers (using a simple arithmetic operation) — and verify each sub-pattern against both given examples before applying it to the new term.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double check the letter-shift and number-shift rules against *both* given examples (not just one) to avoid coincidental false patterns.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some balls are hens.

All vans are hens.

Conclusion (I) : Some balls are vans.

Conclusion (II) : All hens are vans.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: Some balls are hens. All vans are hens.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Draw a Venn diagram: 'hens' is a large set. 'Balls' overlaps partially with 'hens' (Some balls are hens). 'Vans' is entirely contained inside 'hens' (All vans are hens).

 

• Conclusion (I): 'Some balls are vans' — Both 'balls' and 'vans' are related to 'hens', but there is no information linking balls and vans directly to each other; they could overlap or not overlap at all within the 'hens' circle. This does not necessarily follow.

 

• Conclusion (II): 'All hens are vans' — The statement only tells us 'All vans are hens' (vans ⊆ hens); it does not say the reverse. A universal statement cannot simply be converted (reversed) as a certainty. This does not follow.

 

• Since neither conclusion is a guaranteed logical consequence, the answer is Neither (I) nor (II) follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Remember: an 'All A are B' statement can never be validly reversed to 'All B are A' — this is one of the most common traps in syllogism questions.

 

NOTE

 

• When two different subsets ('balls' and 'vans') are each related only to a common third set ('hens') without any direct statement linking them, no conclusion about their mutual relationship can be drawn with certainty.

question: A, B, C, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. Only one person sits between B and T when counted from the right of B. Only one person sits between T and R when counted from the left of R. Only one person sits between B and U when counted from the right of U. Only two people sit between C and R when counted from the left of R. Only one person sits between A and U when counted from the right of A. Who sits third to the right of S?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. T.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (A, B, C, R, S, T, U) sit around a circular table facing the centre; clues describe relative positions using 'right'/'left' counts.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take positions 0-6 clockwise, with 'right' of a person meaning moving clockwise.

 

• 'Only one person between B and T from the right of B' ⇒ T = B + 2.

 

• 'Only one person between T and R from the left of R' ⇒ T = R − 2, so R = T + 2 = B + 4.

 

• 'Only one person between B and U from the right of U' ⇒ B = U + 2, so U = B − 2 = B + 5.

 

• 'Only two people between C and R from the left of R' ⇒ C = R − 3 = (B+4) − 3 = B + 1.

 

• 'Only one person between A and U from the right of A' ⇒ U = A + 2, so A = U − 2 = (B+5) − 2 = B + 3.

 

• Setting B = 0: B=0, C=1, T=2, A=3, R=4, U=5, and the only unused position is 6, so S = 6.

 

• Clockwise seating order: B(0) - C(1) - T(2) - A(3) - R(4) - U(5) - S(6).

 

• Third to the right (clockwise) of S(6): 6 + 3 = 9, and 9 mod 7 = 2, which is T.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert every 'X persons between P and Q, counted from the right/left of one of them' clue into a simple algebraic position equation (add the count+1 in the stated direction), fix one person's position as 0, then solve all equations together to place everyone uniquely.

 

NOTE

 

• Keep a consistent direction convention (here, 'right' = clockwise) throughout the entire problem — mixing conventions midway is the most common source of error in circular arrangement puzzles.

question: John ranked 21st from the bottom and 33rd from the top in his class. How many students are there in his class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 53.

 

GIVEN

 

• John's rank from the bottom = 21st; rank from the top = 33rd.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total students = (Rank from top) + (Rank from bottom) − 1, since John himself is counted once in both ranks.

 

• Total = 33 + 21 − 1 = 53.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Formula: Total = (Rank from top + Rank from bottom) − 1 — always subtract 1 to avoid double-counting the person's own position.

 

NOTE

 

• Forgetting to subtract 1 is the most common mistake in this classic ranking problem — always subtract the overlap of the person counted in both ranks.

question: Himesh starts from Point A and drives 4 km towards the south. He then takes a left turn, drives 7 km, turns right and drives 6 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 7 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 3 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only, unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 7 km towards north.

 

GIVEN

 

• Starting at A, facing South: 4 km South → left turn, 7 km → right turn, 6 km → right turn, 7 km → right turn, 3 km, stopping at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take North as +y, East as +x. Starting direction: South.

 

• Leg 1: 4 km South → position (0, −4).

 

• Left turn from South → facing East. Leg 2: 7 km East → position (7, −4).

 

• Right turn from East → facing South. Leg 3: 6 km South → position (7, −10).

 

• Right turn from South → facing West. Leg 4: 7 km West → position (0, −10).

 

• Right turn from West → facing North. Leg 5: 3 km North → position (0, −7).

 

• Point P is at (0, −7), i.e. 7 km south of A, with no east-west offset.

 

• To return from P(0,−7) to A(0,0), Himesh must travel 7 km towards the north.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net the North-South legs and East-West legs separately: North-South legs (4S, 6S, 3N) net to 7 km South; East-West legs (7E, 7W) exactly cancel to 0 — so the return trip is simply 7 km North.

 

NOTE

 

• With a person facing South, a left turn leads to East and a right turn leads to West (and vice versa on subsequent turns) — always re-derive the new facing direction carefully at each step rather than assuming a fixed pattern.

question:
Refer to the following series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single digit numbers only). Counting to be done from left to right only.

(Left) 9 1 9 1 1 5 4 2 2 9 4 3 9 3 7 1 1 6 7 3 2 2 2 7 4 6 7 (Right)

How many such odd numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by an even number and also immediately followed by an even number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 9 1 9 1 1 5 4 2 2 9 4 3 9 3 7 1 1 6 7 3 2 2 2 7 4 6 7 (27 terms).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan the series for an odd number that has an even number immediately before it AND an even number immediately after it.

 

• At position 10 (value 9): preceded by 2 (even) and followed by 4 (even) → qualifies.

 

• At position 24 (value 7): preceded by 2 (even) and followed by 4 (even) → qualifies.

 

• Checking every other odd number in the series (positions 1,3,4,5,6,12,13,14,15,16,17,19,20,25,27) shows at least one neighbour is odd or the number is at an edge, so they do not qualify.

 

• Total qualifying odd numbers = 2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Write E (even) or O (odd) below every term first — this converts the problem into simple pattern-spotting for 'E O E' triplets, which is much faster and less error-prone than checking raw digits repeatedly.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember that the very first and very last terms of the series can never qualify (they don't have both a preceding and a following term).

question:
What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?

21 ÷ 5 − 25 + 180 × 3 = ?
